Spiich is AI for revenue teams that win on relationships. It automatically updates your CRM after every call, generates daily meeting briefs, drafts follow-up emails, and prospects new leads, saving sales reps 9+ hours per week. Second, the meeting agent automatically prepares meeting briefs, records calls, drafts follow-up emails and updates the CRM. Third, background agents work autonomously on long-running tasks, like finding new leads and analyzing your CRM. See the three ways you use Spiich . What CRMs does Spiich integrate with? It's used by sales reps, SDRs, account executives and the sales leaders who run them, across industries including SaaS, fintech, healthtech and professional services. See customer case studies . Spiich’s agents look in three places: accounts you have never spoken to, customers you already have, and deals you lost. Each opportunity is researched and ranked, and what the agents find is written into your CRM, ready to work. For one team, that meant 3x market coverage in a week . See how to set up a lead generation agent . How does Spiich qualify leads against our ICP? Spiich’s agents score each account against your ideal customer profile (ICP) and write the result to a CRM field you name, such as an ICP fit rating, so reps work the best fits first. An admin writes the ICP in the Target Customer field under Agent Customization, and Spiich uses it for qualification, scoring and prospecting. Agents go beyond firmographics such as size and industry and look for signs that an account has the problem right now: hiring, funding news, blog content and LinkedIn activity. See how to set your ICP . How do I find the decision-maker at a target account? Spiich’s Buyer Discovery agent finds the people who decide at an account and writes them into your CRM, as contact records or as a note on the deal. It maps who sits where and looks for budget authority and active buying signals, not just job titles, and it can run every time a new deal is created. Reps can also ask in chat, and at Rebaba that cut finding the right person from weeks of research to two prompts . See how to create a background agent . How can I find upsell opportunities in my existing customers? Spiich’s agents surface the customers showing real intent to buy more, so reps reach out with a reason rather than a routine check-in. Start from the Key Account Monitoring template and upload your account list, and Spiich sets up a background agent that runs on a schedule and watches exactly those accounts. It can read what your CRM, email and meetings hold on each account, then research the company and the champions inside it for new signals such as hiring, funding news or LinkedIn activity. See how to build an agent from a template . How do I re-engage closed-lost deals? Spiich’s agents check your closed-lost deals for signs that the timing has changed, so reps step back in where the relationship is already warm. Point a background agent that runs on a schedule at the deals in your closed-lost stage, and it can read each deal’s history in your CRM, email and meetings, then research the company for new signals such as funding news, hiring or LinkedIn activity. It flags the deals worth reopening with a note or a task on the deal. See how to point a scheduled agent at a set of records . Does Spiich replace Apollo or our data provider? For most teams, yes: Spiich searches LinkedIn, the web and proprietary databases, then ranks what it finds against your ideal customer profile (ICP) and writes it into your CRM. In practice, prospect research runs up to 12x faster . If you already have a data provider, Spiich works alongside it. See how to bring your own data provider . More of what Spiich does . How can I get sales analytics and insights from our CRM data? Spiich first fills in the CRM: recorded meetings become notes and CRM updates, reps say anything else out loud, and each rep’s connected inbox is read alongside the CRM. On that data, Spiich writes a deal close-likelihood score to a CRM field after a recorded meeting, and the Sales Performance Analysis agent sends a monthly leadership report on what drives revenue, where deals are lost and whether the ideal customer profile (ICP) still holds. The report is read-only research: it does not update CRM records, create tasks or send outreach. See how to set up the Sales Performance Analysis . How does Spiich find what our sales team should repeat or change? Spiich’s Sales Performance Analysis agent reads the CRM history, notes, meeting transcripts and connected email behind your deals, then compares what happened in the deals that closed with the ones that did not. Its monthly report states what the team should repeat or change, using individual deals as evidence for team-wide findings, and links each finding to the original sources and the counterexamples it was tested against. See the monthly Sales Performance Analysis . Can AI do a win-loss analysis of our deals? Spiich’s Sales Performance Analysis agent writes a monthly report on what helps the team win and grow accounts and what costs it business, reading the CRM history, meeting transcripts and connected email behind won and lost deals, including expansion and renewals. The report keeps patterns found in a few researched deals apart from team-wide figures such as win rate, which need the whole accessible deal population. Between reports, you can ask Spiich in chat which deals were won and lost this month and whether the losses share a reason. See prompts for pipeline and win-loss questions . How do I check whether our ideal customer profile (ICP) is still right? Check the ideal customer profile (ICP) against the customers who actually buy, renew and grow. Spiich’s Sales Performance Analysis agent looks across new business, expansion, renewals and repeat purchases to show which customers drive revenue, where the team loses them and whether the ICP still holds. It chooses how far back to look from sales cycles, available outcomes and changes in pricing, customer mix or sales approach, and can compare earlier and recent performance, including an earlier approach that worked better. See how the analysis chooses its history . Can AI score how likely a deal is to close? After a recorded sales meeting, Spiich writes a close-likelihood score to a field in your CRM, derived from the meeting, the emails, the CRM history and web research. Each workspace chooses whether the score appears as a percentage, a band or a qualitative verdict. Spiich publishes no accuracy figure for the score. Do we need to change how we work for the data to be complete? No. Each rep connects Gmail or Outlook once, and Spiich reads that mailbox with read-only access. Meetings recorded by the Spiich Recorder, or transcripts brought in from Fathom, Fireflies or Google Meet, become meeting notes and CRM updates, and anything else can be said out loud instead of typed. zh.summary: 围绕潜客、会后跟进和 CRM 数据构建销售代理工作流。
zh.judgment: 价值在减少销售行政负担且提高有效成交，不是单纯增加触达。
zh.replaces: 销售手工找账户与决策人，记会谈笔记，更新 CRM 并安排下一步。
zh.product: 产品页明确区分建管道、推进交易与收入洞察，官网说明会后回写与跟进草稿。不同模块输出不同，不能把找到更多联系人当作更高收入。
zh.customer: B2B 销售代表与收入管理团队是用户，销售负责人是合理买方推断。重复的 CRM 更新有高频成本，但采购需要证明它不会增加错误触达和数据噪声。
zh.workflow: 公司描述按 ICP 找账户与决策人、写入 CRM；会后记录、生成任务与草拟跟进；再从数据判断有效做法。代表发送及管理者判断仍需要清晰控制。
zh.business_model: 官网有免费开始和销售入口，本次未取得公开定价。团队订阅或按模块合同需确认，数据采购、邮件读取与客户系统实施会影响毛利。
zh.traction: 已检索到具名客户故事和效率主张，属于公司与客户自报。缺少独立对照和真实成交归因，演示中的 CRM 数据也不能当作生产客户结果。
zh.moat: 工作流写回与客户历史数据可能增加粘性。CRM 原生功能、销售数据工具及会议助手都是替代；真正优势应是可用数据和跟进质量共同改善。
zh.funding_read: 资金可推进产品与集成，下一里程碑应是同团队多个模块的持续采用。客户保留是否覆盖数据与实施成本，比早期展示的速度更重要。
zh.risks: 错认决策人、过期账户或错误记录可能污染 CRM，过量跟进会损害关系。跨邮件和日历权限还需与团队实际角色对应。
zh.takeaway: 从销售已有工作节奏接入，把发现、记录与下一行动连起来。先提升 CRM 可信度，再在其上做预测和收入洞察。
zh.watch_next: 看人工改写、CRM 完整性、有效会面与成交率。分开记录行政时间节省和商业结果，并追踪模块续约。

en.summary: Sales agents joining pipeline discovery, follow-up and CRM records.
en.judgment: Less administration and better useful sales outcomes matter more than greater outreach volume.
en.replaces: Finding accounts, identifying decision makers, writing notes and updating CRM manually.
en.product: Product pages separate pipeline building, deal progression and revenue insight, with write-back and follow-up drafts. More contacts do not establish greater revenue.
en.customer: B2B representatives and revenue teams are users; sales leaders are plausible buyers. Frequent CRM work creates cost, but procurement needs evidence of less noise rather than more unwanted outreach.
en.workflow: The described flow matches accounts to an ICP, adds decision makers, records meetings and tasks, drafts follow-ups and analyzes patterns. Sending and managerial decisions need clear controls.
en.business_model: Free-start and sales entries exist, but public pricing was not retrieved. Team or module contracts require confirmation; data acquisition and implementation affect margin.
en.traction: Named stories and efficiency statements are company/customer reports. Independent conversion attribution is missing, and demonstration CRM records are not production outcomes.
en.moat: Write-back and historical context may create continuity. CRM-native tools, prospecting platforms and meeting assistants compete; usable records and follow-up quality should improve together.
en.funding_read: Funding supports product and integrations. Persistent multi-module use within a team is a milestone, evaluated against data and delivery costs.
en.risks: Wrong people or stale records can pollute CRM; excessive follow-up harms relationships. Inbox and calendar permissions should reflect actual team roles.
en.takeaway: Connect discovery, records and next action within existing sales cadence. Improve CRM trust before adding forecasts and revenue insights.
en.watch_next: Watch rewrites, completeness, useful meetings, conversion and module renewals. Separate administrative time saved from commercial outcomes.
